429:         ----------
430:         X : array-like of shape (n_ts, sz, d)
431:             Time series dataset
432: 
433:         Returns
434:         -------
435:         numpy.ndarray of integers with shape (n_ts, n_segments, d)
436:             SAX-Transformed dataset
437:         """
438:         self._is_fitted()
439:         X = check_array(X, allow_nd=True, force_all_finite=False)
440:         X = check_dims(X, X_fit_dims=tuple(self._X_fit_dims_),
441:                        check_n_features_only=True)
442:         return self._transform(X, y)
443: 
444:     def distance_sax(self, sax1, sax2):
445:         """Compute distance between SAX representations as defined in [1]_.
446: 
447:         Parameters
448:         ----------
449:         sax1 : array-like
450:             SAX representation of a time series
451:         sax2 : array-like
452:             SAX representation of another time series
453: 
454:         Returns
455:         -------
456:         float
457:             SAX distance
458: 
459:         References
460:         ----------
461:         .. [1] J. Lin, E. Keogh, L. Wei, et al. Experiencing SAX: a novel
462:            symbolic representation of time series.
463:            Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery, 2007. vol. 15(107)
464:         """
465:         self._is_fitted()
466:         return cydist_sax(sax1, sax2,
467:                           self.breakpoints_avg_, self._X_fit_dims_[1])
468: 
469:     def distance(self, ts1, ts2):
470:         """Compute distance between SAX representations as defined in [1]_.
471: 
472:         Parameters
473:         ----------
474:         ts1 : array-like
475:             A time series
476:         ts2 : array-like
477:             Another time series
478: 
479:         Returns
480:         -------
481:         float
482:             SAX distance
483: 
484:         References
485:         ----------
486:         .. [1] J. Lin, E. Keogh, L. Wei, et al. Experiencing SAX: a novel
487:            symbolic representation of time series. Data Mining and Knowledge
488:            Discovery, 2007. vol. 15(107)
489:         """
490:         sax = self.transform([ts1, ts2])
491:         return self.distance_sax(sax[0], sax[1])
492: 
493:     def inverse_transform(self, X):
494:         """Compute time series corresponding to given SAX representations.
495: 
496:         Parameters
497:         ----------
498:         X : array-like of shape (n_ts, sz_sax, d)
499:             A dataset of SAX series.
500: 
501:         Returns
502:         -------
503:         numpy.ndarray of shape (n_ts, sz_original_ts, d)
504:             A dataset of time series corresponding to the provided
505:             representation.
506:         """
507:         self._is_fitted()
508:         X = check_array(X, allow_nd=True, force_all_finite=False)
509:         X = check_dims(X, X_fit_dims=(None, None, self._X_fit_dims_[-1]),
510:                        check_n_features_only=True)
511:         X_orig = inv_transform_sax(
512:                 X,
513:                 breakpoints_middle_=self.breakpoints_avg_middle_,
514:                 original_size=self._X_fit_dims_[1]
515:         )
516:         return self._unscale(X_orig)
517: 
518:     def _more_tags(self):
519:         tags = super()._more_tags()
520:         tags['_xfail_checks'].update({
521:             "check_transformer_preserve_dtypes" : "Forces int transform"
522:         })
523:         return tags
524: 
525:     def __sklearn_tags__(self):
526:         # Needed for check_estimator_tags_renamed
527:         return super().__sklearn_tags__()
528: 
529: 
530: class OneD_SymbolicAggregateApproximation(SymbolicAggregateApproximation):
531:     """One-D Symbolic Aggregate approXimation (1d-SAX) transformation.
532: 
533:     1d-SAX was originally presented in [1]_.
534: 
535:     Parameters
536:     ----------
537:     n_segments : int (default: 1)
538:         Number of PAA segments to compute.
539:         
540:     alphabet_size_avg : int (default: 5)
541:         Number of SAX symbols to use to describe average values.
542:         
543:     alphabet_size_slope : int (default: 5)
544:         Number of SAX symbols to use to describe slopes.
545:         
546:     sigma_l : float or None (default: None)
547:         Scale parameter of the Gaussian distribution used to quantize slopes.
548:         If None, the formula given in [1]_ is
549:         used: :math:`\\sigma_L = \\sqrt{0.03 / L}` where :math:`L` is the
550:         length of each segment.
551:     
552:     scale: bool (default: False)
553:          Whether input data should be scaled for each feature of each time 
554:          series to have zero mean and unit variance.
555:          Default for this parameter is set to `False` in version 0.4 to ensure
556:          backward compatibility, but is likely to change in a future version.
557: 
558:     Attributes
559:     ----------
560:     breakpoints_avg_ : numpy.ndarray of shape (alphabet_size_avg - 1, )
561:         List of breakpoints used to generate SAX symbols for average values.
562:     breakpoints_slope_ : numpy.ndarray of shape (alphabet_size_slope - 1, )
563:         List of breakpoints used to generate SAX symbols for slopes.
564: 
565:     Notes
566:     -----
567:         This method requires a dataset of equal-sized time series.
568: 
569:     Examples
570:     --------
571:     >>> one_d_sax = OneD_SymbolicAggregateApproximation(n_segments=3,
572:     ...         alphabet_size_avg=2, alphabet_size_slope=2, sigma_l=1.)
573:     >>> data = [[-1., 2., 0.1, -1., 1., -1.], [1., 3.2, -1., -3., 1., -1.]]
574:     >>> one_d_sax_data = one_d_sax.fit_transform(data)
575:     >>> one_d_sax_data.shape
576:     (2, 3, 2)
577:     >>> one_d_sax_data
578:     array([[[1, 1],
579:             [0, 0],
580:             [1, 0]],
581:     <BLANKLINE>
582:            [[1, 1],
583:             [0, 0],
584:             [1, 0]]])
